rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for trying to win someone’s favour by pleasing them.

example.english: They are always buying me snacks to ingratiate themselves with me.
example.traditional: 佢成日買啲小食畀我，想討好我。
example.jyutping: keoi5 seng4 jat6 maai5 di1 siu2 sik6 bei2 ngo5 soeng2 tou2 hou2 ngo5

rows.note: Use this when the flattering is conspicuously sycophantic or self-serving, especially toward someone influential.

example.english: They were blatantly sucking up to the boss in front of everyone to ingratiate themselves.
example.traditional: 佢當住大家面前猛咁擦鞋，睇到人都尷尬。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dong1 zyu6 daai6 gaa1 min6 cin4 maang5 gam3 caat3 haai4 tai2 dou2 jan4 dou1 gaam3 gaai3

rows.note: Use this for ingratiating yourself with someone, often by flattering or courting a person with power or status.

example.english: They keep treating the manager to meals, clearly trying to ingratiate themselves with him.
example.traditional: 佢成日請經理食飯，明顯係想巴結佢。
example.jyutping: keoi5 seng4 jat6 ceng2 ging1 lei5 sik6 faan6 ming4 hin2 hai6 soeng2 baa1 git3 keoi5
